README: CANONICAL origin-key vectors. Dart, Swift and Kotlin all read THIS file at test time. Do not transcribe these values into a test in any language: three copies is three chances to drift, and a drift re-keys every origin and re-grants the retention window silently. Regenerate with `dart run tool/genvec.dart` from packages/stride_health.
algorithm: FNV-1a 64-bit over salt || 0x1F || utf8(identifier), big-endian, 8 bytes. The empty identifier yields ZERO bytes, not eight zeroes.

vectors.why: a second source on one device must not collide with the first
UTF-8 handling of a longer identifier
a display name keys like anything else. It must never be SENT, but if one ever is, it must not survive recognisably
the empty identifier is ZERO bytes on the wire, not eight zero bytes
the same source under a second salt must key differently, or the salt is not mixed in and this is a bare digest
a salt with high bytes. Swift Int64 and Kotlin Long are signed, and an arithmetic shift where a logical one belongs is the likeliest native defect here
a one-byte salt, so the separator must be present: salt||id must not be able to collide with salt2||id2

negativePrivacyVectors.why: 5 bytes — shorter than the key width
